desc: Define direction vectors in clockwise order and verify the clockwise-turn mapping (d+1)%4 against the examples (Ex1: d2→d3, Ex2: d3→d0 confirmed).

Design helper: for fixed direction d and parity p, compute dp[i][j] = longest valid run starting at (i,j) moving along d with expected value (2 if p==1 else 0), processing cells in reverse traversal order.
Implement f[d][p] tables (directions [(-1,-1),(-1,1),(1,1),(1,-1)]) as flat 2D lists, O(nm) per table, 8 passes total.

Implement main loop: for each cell ==1 and each direction d, walk k=0,1,... while values match; at each k compute turn candidate k+1 + f[(d+1)%4][(k+1)%2][next] and no-turn candidate k+1; track global max.
Handle edge cases: single cell with 1 → 1, no 1s → 0, turn immediately after the 1 (k=0), turn at last cell of arm, single row/column grids.

Test against all four provided examples plus custom edge cases (all zeros, all twos with one 1, turn at boundary, single row/column grids); confirmed outputs 5, 4, 5, 1 and correct clockwise-only turn behavior.
Confirm complexity: 8 DP passes O(nm) + walk cost bounded by O(4·nm) since runs from 1s on the same diagonal are disjoint; memory 8·n·m ints acceptable for 500×500.
